items.stem: In a test-driven workflow, why confirm the new test fails before writing the implementation?

options.text: A test that does not fail first may be asserting nothing or already satisfied, giving false confidence
options.rationale: Correct: a failing-first test proves it actually exercises the new behaviour.

options.text: Failing tests run faster than passing ones
options.rationale: Execution speed is not the reason.

options.text: A test must fail at least once to be committed
options.rationale: There is no such mechanical rule; the point is validity.

options.text: Claude Code refuses to implement until a test fails
options.rationale: This is a discipline, not a tool restriction.

items.explanation: Correct: a failing-first test proves it actually exercises the new behaviour.

items.stem: Which TWO describe correct regression repair from a bug report? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Reproduce the bug as a failing test before fixing it
options.rationale: Correct: a reproduction test proves the bug and guards against regression.

options.text: Confirm the whole suite still passes after the fix
options.rationale: Correct: the fix must not break other behaviour.

options.text: Fix the code and skip adding a test to save time
options.rationale: Without a test the bug can silently return.

options.text: Delete the failing scenario from the backlog
options.rationale: Removing the report does not fix or guard the defect.

items.explanation: Correct: a reproduction test proves the bug and guards against regression.
items.domain_ref: Regression repair from a bug report

items.stem: A test passes whether or not the function under test is called. This test is:

options.text: Tautological and untrustworthy; it should be repaired or removed
options.rationale: Correct: a test that cannot fail provides no protection.

options.text: Ideal because it never breaks the build
options.rationale: A test that never fails gives false confidence.

options.text: Fine as long as coverage numbers rise
options.rationale: Coverage from a meaningless test is misleading.

options.text: A good smoke test by design
options.rationale: A smoke test still asserts something meaningful.

items.explanation: Correct: a test that cannot fail provides no protection.
